guides.title: Garbage & Recycling
guides.body:
Curbside garbage and recycling are collected by Cali Carting. Fair Lawn is split into 5 sections; your section sets your days. Find your street (and block range/odd-even side) in the 'Section List by Street' on fairlawn.org/recycling. Your 'block' is the first part of your address (8-01 Fair Lawn Ave is on the 8 block).

Weekly days by section:
- Section 1: Recycling Tue, Garbage Wed (2nd garbage Sat in summer)
- Section 2: Recycling Wed, Garbage Thu (2nd garbage Mon)
- Section 3: Recycling Fri, Garbage Mon (2nd garbage Thu)
- Section 4: Recycling Thu, Garbage Tue (2nd garbage Fri)
- Section 5: Recycling Mon, Garbage Fri (2nd garbage Tue)

Recycling alternates weekly: Paper/Cardboard one week, Bottles/Cans (commingled) the next. Check the 2026 Recycling Calendar for your section's P (paper) and C (cans) weeks. The second weekly garbage pickup runs only in the warm season (the borough page says first full week of May through last full week of September).

Set-out rules:
- Put recycling out after 6 PM the night before and by 6 AM collection day. NO plastic bags for recycling.
- Containers 20-40 gallons, max 40 lbs when full. No limit on recycling quantity.
- Garbage: up to 4 barrels per house per day, lidded 20-40 gal cans, no loose bags or boxes. Remove cans from the curb by midnight after collection.

What goes in recycling:
- Paper/Cardboard: newspapers, magazines, junk mail, cereal boxes, cardboard, office/shredded paper, soft-cover books. No pizza boxes, Styrofoam or plastic wrap.
- Bottles/Cans: glass bottles & jars, aluminum and tin cans, clean foil, plastic bottles/jars/jugs, family-size food tubs, wax-coated gable-top cartons. Rinse out food.

Missed pickup? Call Cali Carting at 201-991-5400. If weather cancels collection, the borough emails/posts a notice; there is no make-up day.

Recycling Center: 20-05 Saddle River Road, Mon-Fri 7:00 AM-3:20 PM, Sat 9:00 AM-12:50 PM, Sun noon-3:50 PM (per 2026 calendar; the website lists slightly different weekend hours, so call 201-794-5341 to confirm). Accepts all curbside recyclables plus electronics, scrap metal, appliances, yard waste, tires (limits apply), used clothing and plastic toys. No garbage, hazardous waste or brick/concrete/dirt.

Holidays: collection is cancelled on Borough holidays marked 'H' on the calendar with no make-up day. Remaining 2026: Thanksgiving Thu Nov 26 and Christmas Fri Dec 25.

guides.title: Bulk, Leaf & Special Pickups
guides.body:
Furniture and bulky items:
- One piece of furniture per residence per garbage day, no appointment needed.
- One toilet per garbage day.
- Carpet: cut and tied in 3-foot lengths, one room per garbage day.

Metal, appliances and electronics: curbside pickup on your recycling day by appointment only. Call the Recycling Office at 201-794-5341 at least one business day ahead. Remove refrigerator doors. Or bring them to the Recycling Center. Computers, monitors, phones, printers, DVD players and game consoles are accepted at the Center; don't cut TV cords. Projection/console TVs go in the garbage.

Construction debris: not taken with regular garbage except on two 'D' days per year (small amounts, up to 4 barrels / 200 lbs, on your garbage day). Fall 2026 D days fall the week of Oct 19-23 (e.g., Section 3 Mon Oct 19, Section 4 Tue Oct 20, Section 1 Wed Oct 21, Section 5 Fri Oct 23; Section 2 on its Thursday garbage day - check the calendar). Otherwise use a contractor, rent a dumpster (street dumpster permit from DPW, 201-794-5304), or buy $50 vouchers at the Recycling or DPW office to drop off at the Recycling Center (car 1 voucher, trailer 2, SUV/van/pickup 3).

Yard waste, leaves and brush: collected with recycling on your recycling day ('Y' on the calendar, roughly April through early December). Use paper leaf bags or containers under 40 gallons; no plastic bags. Branches max 3 ft long and 3 in diameter, bundled and tied. No logs or stumps. Don't rake leaves into the street. The DPW also runs a fall loose-leaf collection; the 2026 loose-leaf schedule was not found online - watch Nixle/email alerts or call DPW at 201-794-5304.

Christmas trees: collected in January on a designated recycling day marked 'X' (in 2026 it was the second full week of January). Remove all ornaments and tinsel; no bags. Check the 2027 calendar when released.

Household hazardous waste (paint, chemicals, propane, pesticides, pool chemicals) is not accepted by the borough. Use Bergen County Utilities Authority (BCUA) collection days, 9 AM-3 PM, rain or shine. Next 2026 date: Sat Nov 14, 2026 at BCUA, foot of Empire Blvd., Moonachie (back gate entry). BCUA info: bcua.org, 201-807-5825.

Free compost is available at the Recycling Center when supplies allow (2 barrels/week).

guides.title: Moving to Fair Lawn Checklist
guides.body:
Welcome to Fair Lawn (Bergen County, ZIP 07410). Borough Hall is at 8-01 Fair Lawn Avenue, (201) 796-1700.

- Water: Fair Lawn runs its own water utility. Call the Water Billing Office at (201) 794-5334 to put the account in your name and arrange a final/initial reading. Sign up for e-billing at fairlawn.org/email-water-billing.
- Electric & gas: PSE&G, 1-800-436-7734 (nj.pseg.com).
- Internet/TV: Optimum (NJ 973-230-6048) or Verizon Fios (1-800-837-4966).
- Garbage & recycling: look up your section and pickup days at fairlawn.org/recycling and download the current Recycling Calendar. Use lidded 20-40 gallon cans.
- Alerts: text 07410 to 888777 or register at local.nixle.com/signup/widget/i/856 for borough Nixle alerts; sign up for email notices via the borough's Constant Contact list.
- Pets: license dogs and cats over 6 months with Human Services (201-794-5327); rabies proof required.
- Voting: update your registration at nj.gov/state/elections (voter-registration) and check your polling place at voter.svrs.nj.gov/polling-place-search.
- Property taxes: due Feb 1, May 1, Aug 1, Nov 1 (10-day grace). Pay online via the borough's Edmunds portal.
- Home resale/CCO: sellers need a Continued Certificate of Occupancy from the Building Department (201-794-5307) and a smoke/CO detector certification (Fire Prevention Bureau, 201-794-5408).
- Landlords must register with the Municipal Clerk (201-794-5340).
- Library card: Maurice M. Pine Library, 10-01 Fair Lawn Ave, 201-796-3400.
- Parking: overnight street parking requires permission from the police (pdlinx.com/parking); commuter lot permits through ParkLync.
- Seniors: free Senior Center membership (201-796-1191) and free borough Mini Bus (201-794-5327).

guides.title: Emergency Alerts & Snow
guides.body:
Emergencies: call 9-1-1. Police non-emergency (24/7): 201-796-1400.

Get alerts:
- Nixle (text/phone/email): text your ZIP code 07410 to 888777, or register at local.nixle.com/signup/widget/i/856. The borough uses Nixle for road closures, weather bulletins, water main breaks and boil-water notices.
- Email notifications: register via the borough's Constant Contact page (lp.constantcontactpages.com/sl/StZKkcy).
- Senior Loop-Line recorded info: (201) 777-6161, updated Fridays.
- Special Needs Registry: residents who may need help in an emergency can file the form on the OEM page (fairlawn.org/emergency-management).

Office of Emergency Management: 201-794-5390. Power outages: PSE&G 1-800-436-7734; gas leak: leave the area, then call PSE&G emergency 1-800-880-7734 or 9-1-1.

Snow rules:
- Clear a path at least 30 inches wide on your sidewalk within 12 hours after snow, sleet or freezing rain stops.
- Do not shovel or blow snow into the street (Borough Code 208-2). Push it onto your lawn.
- Wait for the plow to pass before clearing your driveway apron; plowed snow often ends up there.
- Keep cars off local streets and cul-de-sacs during storms so plows can clear curb to curb.
- Dig out fire hydrants and crosswalks near your home.
- Plowing order: major collector streets, emergency routes and school bus routes first, then residential and cul-de-sac streets.
- Mailboxes and portable basketball hoops damaged in the right-of-way are the owner's responsibility.

DPW (plowing questions): 201-794-5304 or 201-794-5326.

guides.title: Paying Taxes & Water Bills
guides.body:
Property taxes are due quarterly on Feb 1, May 1, Aug 1 and Nov 1. There is a 10-day grace period; after 4 PM on the 10th day, interest is charged back to the 1st (8% on the first $1,500 delinquent, 18% above that). The next due date is Nov 1, 2026 (grace through Nov 10).

Water is billed quarterly by the Borough (2026 rate: $7.50 per 1,000 gallons). Unpaid water bills can lead to shut-off at the curb.

Ways to pay:
- Online (tax and water): wipp.edmundsassoc.com/Wipp/?wippid=0217 (e-check $1.95 fee; card about 2.95%).
- Drop box in the Municipal Building parking lot (no cash).
- By mail with your stub: Tax Collector, 8-01 Fair Lawn Avenue, Fair Lawn, NJ 07410.
- In person at the Tax Collector's office, Mon-Fri 9 AM-4 PM.

Contacts: Tax Collector (201) 794-5338 / 5339; Water Billing (201) 794-5334; Tax Assessor (201) 794-5319 for assessments, $250 senior/disabled and veteran deductions, and appeal info (Bergen County Board of Taxation, due by April 1).

2026 note: final 2026 / preliminary 2027 tax bills were mailed in early August 2026 after the tax rate was certified; the Aug 1 grace period was extended to Sept 1, 2026.

guides.title: Permits
guides.body:
Building/construction permits: Building Department, Room 112, (201) 794-5307. Permits issued 9 AM-4 PM. NJ Uniform Construction Code forms (building, electrical, plumbing, fire, mechanical) are on fairlawn.org/building-zoning; no online permit portal was found.

Zoning permits (Tara Longo, 201-794-5308) - typical fees:
- Fence, shed, patio, driveway (new/replacement), temporary storage bin: $60 (2 copies of survey; 1 for bins).
- Above-ground pool, hot tub, deck, porch, accessory structure, sign: $30.
- In-ground pool, addition, garage, dormer, new house: $45.
- Public sidewalk, apron or curb replacement: $25 (survey + inspection).
- Walkways: zoning approval, no fee.

Other permits and licenses:
- Street dumpster: permit from DPW, (201) 794-5304.
- Home sale: Residential CCO application (Building Dept) and smoke/CO detector certification (Fire Prevention, 201-794-5408).
- Garage/yard sales: no permit, but no signs in the 10-ft right-of-way.
- Landscaper/tree service registration, landlord registration, raffles: Municipal Clerk, (201) 794-5340.
- Dog/cat licenses: Human Services, 201-794-5327.
- Overnight street parking: police, pdlinx.com/parking (one night) or pdlinx.com/parkingpermit (up to a week); hardship permits $10/month via Records Bureau.

Borough code: ecode360.com/FA1754.

guides.title: Getting Around (Transit)
guides.body:
Rail: NJ TRANSIT Bergen County Line stops at two Fair Lawn stations - Broadway (near Broadway/Route 4) and Radburn (Pollitt Drive). Trains connect to Secaucus Junction and Hoboken (transfer at Secaucus for New York Penn Station).

Buses: NJ TRANSIT routes listed for Fair Lawn include 144, 145 and 164 to the Port Authority Bus Terminal, 160 (Garfield/Saddle Brook/Fair Lawn), 171 to the George Washington Bridge, and 770 (local, at Broadway). Check njtransit.com for current schedules.

Commuter parking: train lots at Erie, Upper Erie and Pollitt Dr. Since March 1, 2026 only monthly permits are sold (no daily). Residents and non-residents register via ParkLync (app.parklync.com). Bus commuters can park at the Saddle River Road lot at the DPW yard (20-05 Saddle River Rd), also via ParkLync.

Local options:
- Borough Mini Bus: free for residents 18+, weekdays 9 AM-4 PM within Fair Lawn. Book at 201-794-5327 by 3 PM the prior business day.
- Bergen County Transportation: free rides for medical visits, 201-368-5955.
- Access Link (paratransit): 800-955-2321, option 1.
- FLVAC non-emergency ambulance transport for non-ambulatory residents: 201-797-5321.

guides.title: Voting & Elections
guides.body:
2026 General Election: Tuesday, November 3, 2026, polls open 6 AM-8 PM. Find your polling place at voter.svrs.nj.gov/polling-place-search.

Early in-person voting: Saturday Oct 24 through Sunday Nov 1, 2026, Mon-Sat 10 AM-8 PM, Sun 10 AM-6 PM, at any of Bergen County's 10 sites. Closest to Fair Lawn: Garfield (Nutrition Center/Senior Citizens Building, 480 Midland Ave) and Paramus (Bergen Community College Technology Building, 400 Paramus Rd). Others: Fort Lee, Hackensack, Mahwah, River Vale, Teaneck, Wood-Ridge, Woodcliff Lake, Wyckoff.

Vote by mail: apply through the Bergen County Clerk (201-336-7020). Mailed applications must be received 7 days before Election Day (Oct 27, 2026); in-person applications at the Clerk's office until 3 PM the day before the election.

Register or check registration: nj.gov/state/elections/voter-registration.shtml. Questions: Fair Lawn Municipal Clerk, (201) 794-5340.

guides.title: Seniors & Human Services
guides.body:
Senior Center: 11-05 Gardiner Road (corner of 11th St), (201) 796-1191, srcenter@fairlawn.org. Open Mon-Fri 8-4, Sat 10:30-3:30, Sun noon-3. Free membership for adults 60+; weekday hot lunch at noon (reserve 24 hours ahead).

Human Services (Borough Hall Room 109, 201-794-5327):
- Food Pantry for Fair Lawn residents (applications in English, Russian, Spanish).
- Free Mini Bus within Fair Lawn.
- Housing rehabilitation help for income-eligible homeowners.
- Holiday food and gift drives.
- Referrals: Bergen County Social Services (SNAP, Medicaid), Bergen Community Action Partnership (energy assistance).

Meals on Wheels: Bergen County 201-336-7420; Kosher Meals on Wheels 201-796-5151.
